title: Stream session teardown policy, timeout mitigation, and volatile-output pruning
creator: Priya Raman
description: Problem: When clients disconnect or stall mid-generation we observe several negative outcomes: GPU/worker memory retained by ephemeral KV/prefix caches, partial generations left visible to users or telemetry, increased billing anomalies, and uncertain behavior for function/tool calls encoded into partial structured outputs. This ticket defines a deterministic teardown and pruning policy for streaming sessions to (1) bound resource retention, (2) provide a best-effort resume/inspection workflow, and (3) preserve correctness for structured outputs and tool/function calls across client disconnects, timeouts, and server-initiated aborts. The goal is to ship a safe, observable, and rollout-gated plan that reduces orphaned state by 90% under typical disconnect patterns while maintaining compatibility with older SDKs and streaming clients.
acceptance_criteria: Define session lifecycle states and transitions (ACTIVE, GRACE, QUIESCE, PRUNE, TOMBSTONE) with explicit timeouts
Introduce resume token semantics: short-memory resume (best-effort) that is invalidated by PRUNE/TOMBSTONE
KV/prefix cache memory for a torn session reclaimed within configured soft TTL (default 90s) and hard TTL (default 15m)
No production-visible duplication of tool/function calls when client reconnects with a resume token; duplicate suppression demonstrated in unit and chaos tests
Telemetry: metrics emitting orphaned-session-count, avg-orphan-ttl, prune-rate, resume-success-rate, duplicate-tool-call-count
Canary rollout path with feature-flag and runtime-1.21 toggle; no more than 1% increased error rate in canary infra window
Security review completed for resume tokens (signed, short-lived) and audit logging of partial structured outputs
design_notes: We will introduce a lightweight session-lease object attached to each streaming generation. Lease properties: owner-epoch, last-heartbeat, soft-ttl, hard-ttl, resume-token (HMAC-signed, includes session id + generation seq + expiry). When a client disconnects gracefully or the server detects a timeout, we transition the session to GRACE where KV/prefix caches remain available for a short window (soft-ttl) to support immediate reconnects. After soft-ttl expires we move to QUIESCE: workers stop accepting new input for that session and begin checkpointing minimal resume state (last prefix id + kv checkpoint pointer). After hard-ttl we PRUNE: release GPU memory, drop caches, and write a tombstone event to the session ledger. Tombstones enable fast local routing decisions and ensure resume tokens are invalid. We emit a structured audit entry for any session that contained tool/function call intents to ensure downstream systems can reconcile partially executed external actions.
implementation_plan: 1) API: add optional resume_token field on stream-init response; document semantics and expiry. 2) Runtime: add lease manager per worker group with soft/hard TTL enforcement; new state machine transitions. 3) Storage: compact resume checkpoints to metadata store (low-RPS key) and tombstone events to eventlog. 4) Duplicate suppression: idempotency window keyed by (session, call-id) with in-memory bloom + persistent fallback. 5) Observability: add metrics + dashboards. 6) Migration: default policy off; enable on runtime-1.21 and runtime teams can toggle per-cluster. 7) Tests & chaos: simulate TCP drops, SDK reconnects, and function-call replay scenarios.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease transitions, resume token expiry and validation, duplicate suppression logic for function/tool calls. Integration tests: end-to-end streaming with artificial disconnects (graceful and abrupt) asserting cache retention and reclamation timing. Chaos tests: randomized client disconnects under workload and verification of GPU memory decline after PRUNE. Benchmark: measure impact on median latency and tail latency with resume semantics vs. immediate pruning. Security tests: ensure resume tokens cannot be forged and are logged correctly.
rollout_plan: - Step 1 (canary): enable on 2% of traffic for 48h, monitor stale-session metrics and duplicate-tool-call alerts. - Step 2: extend to 25% if no regressions for 72h. - Step 3: gradual ramp to 100% by config over 2 weeks. Feature flag allow operator to set soft-ttl/hard-ttl per-deployment. Provide emergency 'prune-now' operator runbook to force immediate reclamation for noisy customers.

notes: Compatibility: clients that do not provide resume behavior will be subject to default soft-ttl followed by prune. SDK teams will be given a migration window and example reconnect logic. For structured outputs with pending function calls we will emit an explicit 'partial' envelope with call-id and call-state so customers can correlate and reconcile. All changes behind feature flag until security review and e2e stability gates pass.
